narrative:

The most important reason for this prediction was your class ranking in your third year. You were in the bottom decile of your class, with a rank of 1 out of 10, while admitted students typically rank around 5.79. This was by far the strongest signal, and it pushed the prediction strongly toward bar exam failure. A low third-year rank suggests that your academic performance has not improved over time and may indicate serious difficulty mastering legal material.

While this is a weak positive sign—it actually pushed slightly toward passing—it was not enough to offset your third-year performance. Similarly, your LSAT score of 34 is below the admitted-student average of 37.18, and this also pushed modestly toward passing, meaning your test-taking ability is not the core problem. The main obstacle is your recent academic record.

To improve your chances, focus on your third-year performance. Consider retaking challenging courses, seeking academic support, or gaining practical legal experience. If you reapply later, demonstrating a strong final-year upward trend will be essential to convincing the committee that you can succeed.
